===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=ponder|:inh|enm:thinken<id:ponder>|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*teng-|id=think}}
From {{inh|en|enm|thank|t=gratitude; expression of gratitude, thanks; attractiveness; commendation, praise; God’s grace; goodwill; merit, reward; mind, thought}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|pos=n|id=MED45024}}</ref> from {{inh|en|ang|þanc}}, {{m|ang|þonc|t=gratitude; expression of gratitude, thanks; favour, grace; mind, thought; pleasure, satisfaction}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þankaz|t=gratitude; expression of gratitude, thanks; mind, thought; remembrance}}, ultimately from {{der|en|ine-pro|*teng-|t=to perceive; to think}}.<ref>Compare {{R:OED Online|pos=n|id=9988426071|date=June 2024}}</ref>
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|stq|Tonk|t=thanks}}, {{cog|fy|tanke|t=thanks}}, {{cog|cim|dånke|t=thanks}}, {{cog|nl|dank|t=thanks}}, {{cog|de|Dank|t=thanks}}, {{cog|wym|dank}}, {{m|wym|daŋk}}, {{m|wym|daonk|t=thanks}}, {{cog|yi|דאַנק|t=thanks}}, {{cog|da|tak|t=thanks}}, {{cog|ovd|tokk|t=thanks}}, {{cog|fo|takk}}, {{m|fo|tøkk|t=thanks}}, {{cog|is|takk}}, {{m|is|þökk|t=thanks}}, {{cog|nb,nn|takk|t=thanks}}, {{cog|sv|tack|t=thanks}}, {{cog|got|𐌸𐌰𐌲𐌺𐍃|t=thanks}}, {{cog|xvn|*þank-|t=thanks}}; also {{cog|la|tongeō|t=to know}}.
{{col-bottom}}

For the {{m|en|think}} — {{m|en|thank}} relation, compare typologically {{m+|ru|призна́тельный}} (< {{m|ru|знать}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete}} {{singular of|en|thanks|t=an [[expression]] of [[appreciation]] or [[gratitude]]; [[grateful]] [[feeling#Noun|feelings]] or [[thought#Noun|thoughts]]; [[favor#Noun|favour]], [[goodwill]], [[graciousness]]}}

===Etymology 2===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:thanken|id=verb|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|thanken|t=to express gratitude, give thanks; to congratulate, rejoice with, or wish joy to; to extol; to hold responsible for}},<ref>{{R:MED Online|entry=thanken|pos=v|id=MED45027}}</ref> from {{inh|en|ang|þancian}}, {{m|ang|þoncian|t=to thank}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*þankōn}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þankōną|t=to thank}}, from {{m|gem-pro|*þankaz}} (see [[#Etymology 1|etymology 1]]) + {{m|gem-pro|*-ōną|pos={{glossary|suffix}} forming {{glossary|infinitive}}s of {{glossary|verb}}s from {{glossary|noun}}s}}.<ref>Compare {{R:OED Online|pos=v|id=2185769009|date=June 2024|nodot=1}}; {{R:Lexico|pos=v}}</ref>
{{col-top|2|cog}}
Cognate with {{cog|sco|thank|t=to thank}}, {{cog|stq|tonkje|t=to thank}}, {{cog|cim|dånkan|t=to thank}}, {{cog|nl,de,lb|danken|t=to thank}}, {{cog|wym|danka}}, {{m|wym|daŋka}}, {{m|wym|daonka|t=to thank}}, {{cog|yi|דאַנקען|t=to thank}}, {{cog|da,nb|takke|t=to thank}}, {{cog|fo|takka|t=to thank}}, {{cog|is|þakka|t=to thank}}, {{cog|sv|tacka|t=to thank}}.
{{col-bottom}}

====Alternative forms====
* {{alter|en|thanke||obsolete}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}}
## To [[express#Verb|express]] [[appreciation]] or [[gratitude]] toward (someone or something).
##: {{ux|en|She '''thanked''' him for the lift.}}
##* {{RQ:Erasmus Udall Apophthegmes|chapter=Diogenes|folio=106|para=190|passage=[H]aſt thou no ſhame to deſpiſe that perſone, to whom onely and no man els, thou art bounde to '''thanke''', euen for this veraie pointe, that thou ſetteſt ſo moche by thy peinted ſheathe?}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merry Wives Q1|act=I|scene=i|sig=B|page=15|passage=I can eate no meate, I '''thanke''' you.}}
##* {{RQ:Goldsmith Traveller|page=5|passage=The naked Negro, panting at the line, / Baſks in the glare, or ſtems the tepid vvave, / And '''thanks''' his Gods for all the good they gave.}}
##* {{RQ:Burns Poems|edition=2nd|volume=II|poem=GH|page=66|passage=[S]ae laigh I need na bovv, / For, {{smallcaps|Lord}} be '''thankit''', ''I can plough''; / And vvhen I dovvna yoke a naig, / Then, {{smallcaps|Lord}} be '''thankit''', ''I can beg''; {{...}}}}
##* {{RQ:Scott Tales of My Landlord 2|volume=II|chapter=XII|page=310|passage=That his Majesty has good subjects in England, my Lord Duke, he is bound to '''thank''' God and the laws—that he has subjects in Scotland, I think he may '''thank''' God and the sword.}}
##* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|page=70|passage=She had at once the air of good fellowship and the dignity of a woman, and she seemed to understand Farrar and me perfectly. {{...}} By the time we reached the house we were '''thanking''' our stars she had come.}}
##* {{RQ:Baum Wizard of Oz|page=256|passage=The Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman and the Lion now '''thanked''' the Good Witch earnestly for her kindness, {{...}}}}
##* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|page=97|passage=I told him about everything I could think of; and what I couldn't think of he did. He asked about six questions during my yarn, but every question had a point to it. At the end he bowed and '''thanked''' me once more. As a thanker he was main-truck high; I never see anybody so polite.}}
## ''In the {{glossary|future tense}} in the form'' '''one will thank someone to do something''''', chiefly expressing a command or criticism'': to [[request#Verb|request]] that (someone) [[do#Verb|do]] something.
##: {{ux|en|I’ll '''thank''' you not to smoke in my house!}}
##* {{quote-journal|en|year=1844|month=|title=Art. IV.—''The Public and Private Life of Lord Chancellor [[w:John Scott, 1st Earl of Eldon|Eldon]], including His Correspondence, and Selections from the Anecdote Book, Written by Himself.'' By {{w|Horace Twiss}}, Esq., One of Her Majesty’s Counsel. 3 vols. 8vo. London, 1844. [book review]|editor=w:John Taylor Coleridge|journal=[[w:Quarterly Review|The Quarterly Review]]|location=London|publisher=[[w:John Murray (publishing house)|John Murray]],{{nb...|Albemarle Street}}|volume=LXXIV|issue=CXLVII|page=104|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/sim_quarterly-review-1809_june-october-1844_74_147-148/page/104/mode/1up|oclc=1009026207|passage=Our readers would not '''thank''' us for going into the badgerings which had for some time annoyed the chancellor on the subject of arrears in his court.}}
## {{lb|en|rare}} To express appreciation or gratitude for (something).
## {{lb|en|figurative}}
### To [[respond#Verb|respond]] to (someone) out of, or as if out of, appreciation or gratitude.
###* {{RQ:Scott Kenilworth|volume=III|chapter=I|pages=11–12|pageref=12|passage=I should summon my lord from the Queen's royal presence to do ''your'' business, should I?—I were like to be '''thanked''' with a horse-whip.}}
### ''Chiefly followed by'' '''[[for#Preposition|for]]''': to [[credit#Verb|credit]] or [[hold#Verb|hold]] (someone or something) [[responsible#Adjective|responsible]], especially for something [[negative#Adjective|negative]]; to [[blame#Verb|blame]].
###: {{ux|en|We can '''thank''' global warming for this freak weather.}}
###: {{ux|en|We have two sick newborns to '''thank''' for our lack of sleep lately.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To express gratitude.
